name: LZ
summary: LZ is primarily a dark-matter experiment, but its low-background liquid-xenon target also supports solar-neutrino, coherent-scattering and xenon double-beta-decay studies. It is included here for these documented neutrino channels.
detection_principle: A dual-phase xenon time projection chamber records prompt scintillation and delayed electroluminescence from extracted electrons. Their ratio and reconstructed position separate interaction populations and reduce backgrounds.

results.summary: The technical description establishes the instrument and its broader rare-event programme; channel-specific results must be distinguished from dark-matter limits.
The 5.7 tonne-year analysis reported a solar 8B coherent-scattering signal at 4.5 sigma under the no-dark-matter hypothesis; this is evidence rather than a 5-sigma discovery.

science_scope: This multipurpose dark-matter detector is listed for its neutrino interactions and double-beta-decay programme. A solar-neutrino background estimate, projected sensitivity and an observed neutrino population are different scientific claims.
